construction.name: heterogeneous_complete_staggered_polygon_patch_rows_and_layers
construction.proof:
Forced face-contact staggered columns for octagonal and dodecagonal prisms

Octagon: put a=(1+sqrt(2))/2 and b=1/2. The ideal flat-oriented regular octagon has vertices(+-a,+-b),(+-b,+-a), with |x|,|y|<=a and |x+y|,|x-y|<=a+b. Define the column step h=(3+sqrt(2))/2 and full vertical period v=2a=1+sqrt(2). The owner centers are(h*i,v*j+a*(i mod2)). Owners in one column separate by the horizontal face normal. In neighboring columns their minimal vertical offset is a, and h+a=2(a+b), so a diagonal face normal separates them. Columns two or more apart separate on x since2h>2a. Thus these whole octagons form the classical dense staggered lattice. This is the standard face-contact lattice seen after its forced45-degree symmetry change, not a tuned angle.

Dodecagon: put a=(2+sqrt(3))/2, v=2a and h=sqrt(3)*a=(3+2sqrt(3))/2. The ideal flat-oriented regular dodecagon has apothem a and support normals at integer multiples of30degrees. Use centers(h*i,v*j+a*(i mod2)). One-column pairs separate on y. Neighboring columns at the minimal offset a separate along the30-degree face normal because (sqrt(3)/2)*h+a/2=2a. More distant columns separate on x because2h>2a. These are complete dodecagons in the standard triangular face-contact lattice. The column direction is forced by those face contacts.

For either source, a c-column by r-row patch consists of every whole owner with0<=i<c,0<=j<r. Its exact bounding box dimensions are(v+(c-1)*h,v*r+epsilon*v/2,L), epsilon=1 if c>1 and0 otherwise. Its midpoint is((c-1)*h/2,(r-1)*v/2+epsilon*v/4,0). Both side costs and the unmatched staggered end are retained. The ideal owner frame is fixed at pi/8 for the octagon or pi/12 for the dodecagon relative to the canonical source. No angle is searched.

Apply the complete heterogeneous row/layer rule: for a fixed layer thickness, a row contains floor(S/module_width) identical whole patches; rows of possibly different patch types concatenate with their full row heights. Layers concatenate with their full thicknesses. Keep each proper axis-permutation quaternion and act on the whole patch, including every owner frame. The full backpointer word is an inverse decoder. Distinct boxes have disjoint interiors, and every within-patch pair has the source separator just proved. A named suffix of whole owners may be deleted while retaining its complete parent.

All costs lie in(p+q*sqrt(d))/2 with nonnegative integers p,q, d=2 or3. The finite cost dynamic program retains an actual row/layer word and does not solve a free angle. Binary64 quaternions in native files are a nearby numerical realization with a common outward margin; native certification checks their exact represented rotations, every owner vertex and every pair separately. The ideal source theorem does not silently replace that native check.
construction.cost_convention: Each integer pair[p,q]denotes(p+q*sqrt(2))/2. Every module cost includes both complete patch ends.
construction.native_decoder: Read complete_parent_assembly.word in order as layers; center their summed full thicknesses in z. Read each layer.rows.word in order as complete module rows, centered together in y. A row has module_count identical whole patches centered in x, spaced by its full width. For each a by b patch use local owner centers(pitch*u,period*(v+(u mod2)/2),0)minus midpoint((a-1)*pitch/2,(b-1+epsilon/2)*period/2,0), epsilon=(a>1). Act on local centers by the stored proper module quaternion. The actual owner quaternion is module_quaternion*ideal_origin_quaternion_native. Keep precisely retained_owner_words, multiply all centers by1.0000001, and inflate the common nominal host by that factor plus1e-7.
